title: The Serapeum as a sonohydrogen plant

tellings.quote: ultrasound to break down water molecules to produce hydrogen and oxygen which is my hypothesis for the function of the sarapium.

plain: The Serapeum, an ancient underground site at Saqqara in Egypt, was built to use ultrasound to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, according to a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm. He presents this to Michels as his own hypothesis. It would make the site an ancient fuel plant.
